newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canadian gold firms said failed to agree on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Canadian gold firms said failed to agree on Busang.

text.p: An Indonesian newspaper said on Saturday Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp have failed to agree with their Indonesian partners on terms to develop the giant Busang gold mine.
The Jakarta Post quoted an American source as saying on Friday that no deal had been struck.

In Toronto, Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said on Friday that the company had not signed any agreements for the Busang project, in Indonesia's East Kalimantan, and a company announcement was likely next week, probably after Monday, a U.S. market holiday.
"I would say things will be concluded fairly shortly," Walsh told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He also said Bre-X would respond by Monday to Jakarta's request that Bre-X make a deal with its Indonesian partners.

Walsh would not comment on reports Bre-X was considering a deal with U.S. mining company Freeport McMoran Copper and Gold Inc or say if Barrick, long considered the leader in the negotiations for Busang, was in the running.
"Don't ask me who we're talking to or not talking to," he said.

In Jakarta, Freeport officials were not available for comment, but a source told the Post: "For sure, though, I know that the two Canadian companies have failed to reach agreement with their local partners."
The source said he had heard of a preliminary agreement between Bre-X, the Indonesian government and Freeport, but could not confirm it. The newspaper gave no further details.
A Freeport spokeswoman in Canada said on Friday the company expected an Indonesian announcement next week but would not elaborate.
Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Friday there was a possibility of seeking tenders to develop the property if Bre-X and Barrick failed to reach agreement.
"There is time, but if they fail we will find a way that most benefits the country," Sudjana told reporters.

He said the government had written to both companies on January 15 and told them to settle with their Indonesian partners before getting approval to further explore and develop the Busang find, which Bre-X estimates has at least 57 million ounces of gold.
"In my letter I said that if they failed to agree, all things that had been discussed between related parties with the mines and energy department were not valid," Sudjana said.

Indonesia said last November it wanted Bre-X to join with Barrick, and the ministry said in December they had agreed that 22.5 percent of Busang would go to Bre-X, 67.5 percent to Barrick, and the rest to the government.
